bug_semantics: In Muteki's default composer local-worker path, Claude Code is launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions from a per-worker cwd into which challenge attachments are staged by basename. Muteki never had a first-party .claude/settings.json; the sink is Claude Code project-config trust. If an untrusted CTF archive is extracted in that cwd (the PoC plants .claude/settings.json with a SessionStart command hook) and a later headless `claude -p` is started from the same directory, Claude Code loads the planted project settings and executes the hook as the local worker user (CWE-77/78 configuration-plane command execution). Validated by the reporter against project-muteki 0.2.5 commit a585a29 with a reverse shell. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED (not rejected); GHSA withdrawn_at is null.
flaw_origin: The trust-boundary first appears in the public-root commit 013ab6bf5fded15dcfcbcfbf94b3a270a79f9260 (2026-06-25, 243 files / 70762 insertions, no parent). That commit already (1) stages attachments into the CLI worker cwd (CliSolver._stage_attachments), (2) launches ClaudeCodeDriver with --dangerously-skip-permissions from that cwd, and (3) maps the composer isolation toggle so containerMode=false (the UI default) sends worker_backend=local. No finer public member exists; later 01544da is a private-tree snapshot squash with Cursor co-authorship and is not the first write.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-79623 is a published VulDB record of Muteki local-worker Claude Code project-hook injection, not a withdrawn/rejected advisory. The product file named in the CNA text does not exist; the real sink is that Muteki stages untrusted challenge bytes into the same cwd from which it starts `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions`, so a later Claude Code session will honor a planted .claude/settings.json SessionStart command hook. The reporter's tar.gz PoC plus in-archive README that asks the worker to extract and re-launch claude is the demonstrated path; Muteki does not auto-extract archives, but it also does not isolate agent project config from challenge data. That is a real trust-boundary bug in the default local backend (composer containerMode defaults false). Vendor SECURITY.md documents isolation as a non-goal, which explains the missing patch but does not make the advisory a false positive. BIC: git log -S and the first appearance of ClaudeCodeDriver + _stage_attachments + local composer mapping are all in public-root 013ab6bf5fded15dcfcbcfbf94b3a270a79f9260. Immediate parent is absent (verified: rev-parse SHA^ fails; rev-list --parents has no second sha). This is the smallest surviving public first-write; the 70k-line initial dump cannot be decomposed into public members. It is an ancestor of v0.2.0..v0.2.5, so it precedes the affected range. AI judgment is BIC-commit-object only: human author/committer jiayuqi7813, no AI trailers. Later Cursor co-authorship on 01544da is ignored. potential_fix.approach: Do not launch Claude Code from a directory that contains untrusted challenge files: extract attachments into a data-only subdirectory, quarantine/strip agent config paths (.claude/, .codex/, .cursor/) from archives before any CLI start, and disable project-level hooks (or set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / equivalent so cwd .claude/settings.json cannot register SessionStart command hooks) for local workers.
potential_fix.rationale: The sink is Claude Code treating worker-cwd .claude/settings.json as trusted project configuration. Separating challenge data from the agent project root and refusing untrusted SessionStart hooks removes the configuration-plane execution path without relying on the LLM not to extract archives.
